name: Afar Raidmasters

abilities.name: Sea Sickness
abilities.text: As these men are inexperienced sailors. Caught up in sea combat, they suffer various penalties.

abilities.name: Killing Spree
abilities.text: Increases weapon damage for an extended period.

attributes.name: Disciplined
attributes.text: This unit does not suffer a morale penalty when the general dies. It can also rally after routing more often.

attributes.name: Resistant to Fatigue
attributes.text: Fatigue has less of an effect on this unit.

attributes.name: Hide (forest)
attributes.text: This unit can hide in forests until enemy units get too close.

attributes.name: Scare (everyone)
attributes.text: This unit frightens all enemy units.

attributes.name: Immune to Fear
attributes.text: This unit is immune to the fear effects of scary units.

short: The blink of an eye; the flash of the blade.
history: Referred to as "Han’e" in Ge’ez, the ancient language of Ethiopia, the ‘gile’ is a sickle-like sword. Its curved blade is deadly sharp and was used to strike behind an opponent’s shield at unprotected areas. Unlike the shotel, which it most-closely resembles, both the upper and lower part of the gile's blade is sharpened. As a result, it could be used to slash from side to side or up and down, frequently inflicting mortal wounds in the process. The gile's unusual shape also meant it could be hooked around the top of its bearer’s own shield in order to brace for an incoming charge. Grave goods and art of the period reveals that the sword was popular, and possibly originated, among the northern Ethiopian Afar tribe before spreading across eastern Africa.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
